subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 7: English in action – Saying what you like and don’t like
outcomes: Say what you like and don't like with different expressions.
Order expressions from most positive to most negative.
Put the stress on the correct syllable in animal names.

tf.s: I'm crazy about dolphins means I like dolphins very much.
tf.why: Yes, crazy about is very positive.

tf.s: I can't stand spiders is stronger than I'm not keen on spiders.
tf.why: Yes, can't stand is the most negative.

tf.s: I don't mind ants means I hate ants very much.
tf.why: I don't mind is neutral: it's OK for me.

tf.s: In giraffe, the stress is on the second syllable: gi-RAFFE.
In elephant, the stress is on the last syllable.
tf.why: We say EL-e-phant, stress on the first syllable.

tf.s: In kangaroo, the stress is on the last syllable: kan-ga-ROO.
tf.why: Yes, ROO is the strong part.

tf.s: I quite like is more positive than I'm crazy about.
tf.why: Crazy about is stronger than quite like.

tf.s: In the dialogue, one child is scared of sharks.
tf.why: Yes, sharks scare one of the children.

tf.s: We say: I'm crazy on sea animals.
tf.why: The correct preposition is about: crazy about.

tf.s: I find camels really interesting is a positive sentence.
tf.why: Yes, it shows you like learning about them.

boxes.why: I don't like … at all is very negative.

boxes.q: Do you like ants? – I don't ___ them. (It's OK.)
boxes.why: I don't mind is a neutral answer.

boxes.q: Which expression is the most negative?
boxes.why: Can't stand means you really hate it.

boxes.q: Which expression is the most positive?
boxes.why: Crazy about means you love it.

boxes.q: Where is the stress in dolphin?

boxes.why: We say I'm not keen on …

boxes.q: Which is a question about likes?
Which is a good survey result sentence?
o: Six students are crazy about dolphins.

hunt.q: Animal one child is scared of

mcq.q: Which animals do the children talk about in the dialogue?
o: spiders, ants, sea animals and sharks
mcq.why: These are the animals in the video.

mcq.q: Which list goes from most positive to most negative?
o: crazy about – quite like – don't mind – can't stand
can't stand – don't mind – quite like – crazy about
quite like – crazy about – can't stand – don't mind
don't mind – crazy about – can't stand – quite like
mcq.why: Great! That is the likes scale in order.

mcq.q: What does I'm not keen on … mean?
mcq.why: Not keen on is a soft way to say you don't like it.
The first syllable is strong: EL-e-phant.

mcq.q: Amal loves horses very much. What does she say?
Ali thinks snakes are terrible and he hates them. What does he say?
mcq.why: Can't stand is for things we hate.

mcq.q: Your friend asks: Do you like ants? You think they're OK. What do you say?
o: I don't like them at all.
mcq.why: I don't mind is the neutral answer.
We say keen on, not keen about.

mcq.q: Sara says: I'm not keen on spiders. Huda says: I can't stand spiders. Who dislikes spiders more?
mcq.why: Can't stand is stronger than not keen on.

mcq.q: Why do we clap when we practise animal names?
o: To hear and feel the stressed syllable
mcq.why: Clapping shows which syllable is strong.
